# Francis Ngannou

Francis Ngannou (Francis Zavier Ngannou) is a Cameroonian-French professional fighter, widely regarded as one of the most powerful heavyweight strikers in combat sports history.

## Personal Background
- **Born:** September 5, 1986, in Batié, Cameroon
- **Height:** 6'4" (193 cm)
- **Nickname:** "The Predator"

## Early Life
Ngannou had an extremely difficult childhood. His parents separated when he was young, and he grew up in poverty. By age 10, he worked in a sand quarry to help support his family. He dreamed of becoming a boxer, inspired by Mike Tyson.

At 26, he left Cameroon and traveled through Africa to Europe, attempting to cross via Morocco into Spain. He was reportedly detained and faced harsh conditions before eventually making it to Paris, where he was initially homeless before being directed to the MMA Factory gym by a coach named Didier Carmont, working with trainer Fernand Lopez.

## MMA Career

### UFC
Ngannou signed with the UFC in 2015 and built a reputation for devastating knockouts. Notable moments include:
- A famous knockout of Alistair Overeem in 2017 with an uppercut considered one of the most brutal in UFC history
- Lost his first title shot to Stipe Miocic at UFC 220 (January 2018)
- Won the UFC Heavyweight Championship by knocking out Miocic in the rematch at UFC 260 (March 2021)
- Successfully defended his title against Ciryl Gane at UFC 270 (January 2022) despite a knee injury

His record-setting punch was measured at 129,161 units on a PowerKube, reportedly the hardest punch ever recorded.

### Departure from UFC
In January 2023, Ngannou left the UFC after contract disputes, vacating his title. He cited issues including better fighter pay, healthcare, sponsorship freedom, and the ability to box.

### PFL
In May 2023, he signed with the Professional Fighters League (PFL) as chairman of PFL Africa and a fighter.

## Boxing Career
- **October 28, 2023:** Faced Tyson Fury in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia. Despite being a heavy underdog, he knocked Fury down and lost a controversial split decision.
- **March 8, 2024:** Fought Anthony Joshua, who knocked him out in the second round.

## Personal Life
Tragically, Ngannou's 15-month-old son Kobe passed away in April 2024. He has spoken publicly about his grief.

He is known for his philanthropy, particularly the Francis Ngannou Foundation, which supports children in Cameroon through sports and education.
